source.title: Comparison of cardiovascular and renal outcomes between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in patients with type 2 diabetes without prior cardiovascular or renal disease

atoms.canonical_statement: The study aimed to compare cardiovascular and renal outcomes of dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and DPP-4 inhibitors in patients with type 2 diabetes without prior ASCVD, CKD, or heart failure, and to compare lipid, glycemic, and renal-function changes.

The investigators retrospectively identified patients prescribed empagliflozin, dapagliflozin, or a DPP-4 inhibitor at Seoul National University Bundang Hospital from April 2009 through December 2020.
The medication initiation date for the SGLT2 inhibitor or DPP-4 inhibitor was the index date.
Patients were excluded for type 1 diabetes mellitus.

atoms.canonical_statement: Before propensity-score matching, the eligible exposure groups contained 1,424 dapagliflozin-treated patients, 921 empagliflozin-treated patients, and 10,981 DPP-4 inhibitor controls.

population.label: Eligible pre-match cohort

atoms.canonical_statement: Propensity-score matching used nearest-neighbor matching in a 1:1:2 ratio.

Propensity-score matching included age, sex, 10-year ASCVD risk, systolic blood pressure, microalbuminuria or proteinuria, HbA1c, GFR, antiplatelet therapy, renin-angiotensin system blocker use, and statin use.

After 1:1:2 propensity-score matching, the analytic cohort included 921 dapagliflozin-treated patients, 921 empagliflozin-treated patients, and 1,842 DPP-4 inhibitor controls, for 3,684 patients total.

population.label: Propensity-score-matched cohort of adults with type 2 diabetes without prior ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD as defined by the study

atoms.canonical_statement: One matched exposure group received dapagliflozin.
One matched exposure group received empagliflozin.
The control group received DPP-4 inhibitor therapy.
The 10-year ASCVD risk was calculated with the Pooled Cohort Equations using age, sex, cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, antihypertensive treatment, diabetes, and smoking status.
The study defined composite coronary events as acute coronary syndrome and coronary revascularization.

outcome.definition: Acute coronary syndrome and coronary revascularization

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined composite ischemic events as acute coronary syndrome, coronary revascularization, and stroke.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study defined hospitalization for heart failure as hospitalization for heart failure.
The study defined renal events as renal death, initiation of renal replacement therapy, and admission due to acute kidney injury or ckd progression.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study also assessed serial total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HbA1c, and GFR during follow-up.
Hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals were estimated with Cox proportional-hazards models; two-sided p values below 0.05 were considered statistically significant.
For multivariable Cox models, univariable factors with p values below 0.200 entered stepwise backward elimination.
Median age was 56, 56, and 57 years in dapagliflozin, empagliflozin, and control groups, respectively.

atoms.canonical_statement: Total cholesterol did not differ significantly among the groups during follow-up.
At 24 and 36 months, LDL cholesterol was significantly higher in the empagliflozin group than in the control and dapagliflozin groups.
At 24 and 36 months, HbA1c was significantly lower in the empagliflozin group than in the other groups.
GFR tended to be better preserved at 24 months and was significantly higher at 36 and 48 months in both SGLT2 inhibitor groups than in the DPP-4 inhibitor control group.

The authors concluded that SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with lower risks of ASCVD-related events, heart-failure hospitalization, and renal events than DPP-4 inhibitor use in patients without prior ASCVD, heart failure, or CKD.
The authors reported no statistically significant clinical-outcome differences between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin in this cohort.

The authors interpreted the similar heart-failure, renal, and GFR patterns with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin as support for an SGLT2 inhibitor class effect, while calling for prospective or nationwide real-world comparisons.

The authors observed numerically higher ischemic-event rates with empagliflozin than dapagliflozin but the direct comparisons were not statistically significant; they proposed higher LDL cholesterol as a possible explanation rather than an established mechanism.

The study had a relatively small matched sample, few clinical events, and follow-up that the authors considered too limited to establish differences between dapagliflozin and empagliflozin, especially in a low-risk population.
Because the study was retrospective, laboratory measurements were not prospectively scheduled at fixed intervals; the analysis used more than 16,000 available laboratory results.
Propensity-score matching could not eliminate residual confounding from unmeasured factors.
The authors reported receiving no specific funding for the work.
The authors declared that no competing interests existed.
The study dataset was provided in Supporting Information as S1 Appendix.

The supplied S1 Appendix is a 3,684-row, 50-column patient-level matched-cohort dataset; its group counts are 921 dapagliflozin, 921 empagliflozin, and 1,842 DPP-4 inhibitor controls, and its Table 2 event counts reconcile with the article.
